clue.text: Victoria area rave in church building

parts.note: Vic is the short form of the name Victoria
A is the standard abbreviation for area
to rave is to rage, to rant furiously

explanation.surface: Someone holds a wild party in a church in the Victoria district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rave' suggests a dance party, but here it is the verb meaning to rant.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicarage is the house provided for a parish vicar, a building belonging to the church.

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
each item put up at an auction is a lot

explanation.surface: Someone muttering about a fool's purchase at a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Clot is informal British slang for a stupid person.

parts.note: W is a common abbreviation for with
inner feelings are private, hidden ones

explanation.surface: A champion who keeps a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion is the one who comes first in a contest, the victor.

clue.text: Carnivore and wife having vegans' meal regularly

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of the phrase is kept

parts.note: the even letters of vegans' meal; having is just a joining word in the surface

explanation.surface: A meat-eater and his wife sit down to a vegan dinner, an odd pairing.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'vegans' meal' supplies letters: its 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th and 10th letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The weasel is a small predatory mammal that lives on meat, so it is a carnivore.

clue.text: A call for help about finest insulating material

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the distress signal wraps round the next word

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
the finest is the best

explanation.surface: A distress call goes out about the best insulation to buy.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral once widely used as fireproof and heat insulation.

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
to mature is to age

explanation.surface: A little, well-grown herb plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface also hints at the other sense of the answer, a wise old person.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage is an aromatic plant whose leaves are used in cooking, a kitchen herb.

clue.text: Misfortunes with pelt around part of eg the Malverns?

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the word for pelt is placed on either side

parts.note: a pelt is an animal's skin, its hide
ills are troubles or misfortunes

explanation.surface: Bad luck involving animal skins somewhere in the English hills.
explanation.walkthrough: The Malverns are a range of hills in Worcestershire, England; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Malvern Hills are an example of hills, and the slope of any one is a hillside.

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are set in motion and rearranged

parts.note: OAPs are old-age pensioners, taken as letters

explanation.surface: Pensioners with jobs cleaning a pub bar.
explanation.walkthrough: An OAP is a British old-age pensioner.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar of soap is a solid block used for washing, so a cleaning bar.

indicators.note: after places the word for home behind the word for market

parts.note: a mart is a market
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A man goes home after shopping at the market.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin is a man's name, and a chap is a man, so any male name will do.

clue.text: Viewed spoken part of stage work

indicators.note: spoken tells us to go by how the word sounds when said

parts.note: viewed means seen, which is said the same way

explanation.surface: A spoken section of a play that has been watched.
explanation.definitionFit: Plays are divided into acts and scenes, so a scene is a section of a theatrical work.

indicators.note: trapped in means held inside, so the answer sits within the next word

parts.note: the middle three letters of this word

explanation.surface: A poor sheep has got stuck in a drain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewe is the specific word for a female sheep, so it is a sheep defined by its broader category.

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the club's name is kept

parts.note: the initial of Fulham
a player in a theatre is an actor

explanation.surface: A Fulham footballer's sway over the team.
explanation.walkthrough: Fulham is a London football club, so 'player' looks like a footballer; it is a stage player.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is an element that affects an outcome, something exerting influence.

clue.text: Stream in The Queen — sensational story

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the stream goes within the following word

parts.note: taken as written
a rill is a small brook or stream
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A shocking tale about a brook running through the Queen's land.
explanation.walkthrough: The stream goes inside THE, after its first two letters, and R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A thriller is a novel or film full of suspense and excitement, a sensational story.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a symbol of the alphabet
second meaning: one who lets property

explanation.surface: A description of what the landlord is like as a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' reads as personality, but it is a written symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an alphabetic symbol and, read as let-ter, someone who lets out rooms.

clue.text: Very exciting vote in central Jericho

parts.note: to elect is to vote someone in

indicators.note: central means only the middle letters of the town's name are kept

parts.note: the middle three of its seven letters

explanation.surface: A thrilling election held in the heart of the ancient town of Jericho.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric is used figuratively of an atmosphere charged with excitement.

clue.text: Birds flying around last of the rubbish

indicators.note: around means the jumbled birds enclose the single letter
flying suggests the letters scatter and land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be jumbled

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of the following word is used

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Birds flapping about over the last of the waste at a tip.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the final letter of 'the' is used, leaving 'rubbish' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris means scattered waste and fragments, which is rubbish.

clue.text: Generously treated pilots after a crash

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters are left in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Airmen given lavish care after their plane went down.
explanation.definitionFit: To be spoilt is to be pampered or indulged, treated with excessive generosity.

parts.note: issue is a legal term for offspring

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Kids first needing someone to put out a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a publisher is only one kind of issuer.
explanation.definitionFit: A publisher issues books and magazines, so it is one example of an issuer.

clue.text: Purpose of home with temporary accommodation

parts.note: being in means being at home
a tent is a shelter put up for a short stay

explanation.surface: Choosing between a house and camping out.
explanation.definitionFit: Intent is a noun meaning aim or intention, a synonym of purpose.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an enclosure for animals

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a birdcage, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a female swan and also a small enclosure for keeping livestock.

parts.note: a cell is a small room or chamber

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the preceding word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An instrument heard at the start of a chamber orchestra piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chamber orchestra' looks like one phrase, but the words split: a room, then a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The cello is a large bowed string instrument of the violin family.

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the tin wraps round the letter

parts.note: a tin is a can
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities

explanation.surface: A tin of paint of a shade no one can name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyan is a greenish-blue colour, one of the printing primaries.

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so the word for dull goes in the middle

parts.note: too means also, as well
mat is a variant spelling of matt, without shine

explanation.surface: A fruit that is boring on the inside too.
explanation.walkthrough: Botanically the tomato is a fruit, though it is usually cooked as a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The tomato is the fleshy seed-bearing part of its plant, so technically a fruit.

parts.note: the setter speaking of themself
ET is the film alien, the Extra-Terrestrial

explanation.surface: Someone claims a close encounter with a visitor from space.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet someone is to come across them, an encounter.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pastime of which bridge is one example
second meaning: an amusement or recreation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' and 'diversion' suggest a road detour; bridge here is the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge is one card game among many, and any game is a recreation that diverts the mind.

clue.text: Slips perhaps in heather by North American lake

parts.note: ling is common heather, the moorland plant
Lake Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Someone lost their slips in the heather beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slips' looks like a verb about falling; it is a noun for underskirts, and 'perhaps' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Slips are women's undergarments, one example of lingerie.
